sentences.text: Walterosteus was a small arthrodire placoderm belonging to the family Selenosteidae, found in Late Devonian rocks in Germany and Morocco.
It is classified within the family Selenosteidae and the class Placodermi.
This creature lived during the Frasnian stage of the Devonian period, between 382.31 and 372.15 million years ago.
It is debated whether Walterosteus should be considered a separate genus from Enseosteus, with some researchers arguing that a specific contact between the rostral and pineal plates distinguishes it.
